verdict.rationale: Pipecat backs its 'ultra-low latency' claim with a dedicated STT latency tuning page. That page ships measured P99 latency values per supported STT service and defines Time To Final Segment, and built-in metrics let teams measure latency themselves. The guidance covers the STT and turn-detection stage rather than full voice-to-voice latency. missing for 10: documented end-to-end voice-to-voice latency numbers, tuning guidance covering the LLM/TTS/transport stages, independent benchmark corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can see documented end-to-end voice latency numbers or tuning guidance backing the platform's speed claims

citations.quote: Pipecat ships with measured P99 latency values for each supported service so that turn detection can account for this delay automatically.
Time To Final Segment (TTFS) measures how long it takes from the moment a user stops speaking until the STT service delivers the final transcript.
Pipecat offers built-in metrics for both, which can be enabled with straightforward configuration options.
